title: Diagnose & Fix State Corruption from Index-as-Key
concept: Uncontrolled State Retention across Key Changes
problemStatement: Implement `simulateTodoDeletion(todos, deleteIndex, useStableKey)` that demonstrates why using index as key causes state corruption when items are removed. When `useStableKey` is true, state stays bound to the item's true ID; when false, state stays bound to the array index.
interviewTrap: This is the classic senior interview question: when deleting item 0, the input at index 0 still displays item 0's text if index was used as key!

testCases.name: Stable key preserves correct text on each item after deletion
testCases.input: Delete top item with stable key
testCases.testFn: const todos = [{ id: '1', text: 'Item 1', userTextInInput: 'one' }, { id: '2', text: 'Item 2', userTextInInput: 'two' }]; return simulateTodoDeletion(todos, 0, true);

testCases.name: Index-as-key causes state bleed where remaining item gets deleted item's input state
testCases.input: Delete top item with index as key
testCases.testFn: const todos = [{ id: '1', text: 'Item 1', userTextInInput: 'one' }, { id: '2', text: 'Item 2', userTextInInput: 'two' }]; const res = simulateTodoDeletion(todos, 0, false); return res[0].displayedText;

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: Using array indices as keys (`key={index}`) is a notorious React anti-pattern. When items are inserted, deleted, or reordered, an item's index changes. React compares components by key; if keys remain `0, 1, 2...`, React matches the old index 0 fiber to the new index 0 item, preserving the old fiber's internal state (uncontrolled inputs, stateful hooks) on the WRONG data!
stepByStepWalkthrough: Simulate state corruption caused by index keys during item deletion or unshift.
Detect if `key === index` pattern is being used on stateful components.
Diagnose: When an item is prepended or deleted, component at index 0 retains old internal state because key `0` matched.
Remediate: Replace index keys with stable entity IDs (e.g. `item.id`).
Verify that with stable ID keys, component state remains strictly attached to the correct logical entity across reorders.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: During reconciliation, React uses `(element.key === null ? element.type : element.key)` to find matching fiber nodes in `alternate`. Matching an index key matches the old Fiber node whose `memoizedState` linked list contains the previous item's state values, leading to visual bugs and form input corruption.

complexity.space: O(N) memory for item state tracking.

edgeCasesHandled: Deleting first item with index keys corrupts last item's display.
Migrating to stable ID keys restores 100% state fidelity.
Preserves input field cursor and focus state.

specifications: Robin Pokorny: Index as a key is an anti-pattern (Cited in official React docs)
React Official Docs: Why keys are needed and why indices fail
verifiedRules: Index keys break component state identity when lists are modified.
Stable unique IDs guarantee that Fiber node memoizedState stays bound to the correct entity.
